title: Brand Equity Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 22
description:
Same laddoos inside, two packs: one plain, one with the Laddoo Lab name. Parents still pick Laddoo Lab, again and again. Why does a name change the choice? In this animated lesson we follow Laddoo Lab, a millet laddoo brand from a home kitchen in Bengaluru, to understand brand equity.

You will see Kevin Lane Keller's definition of customer-based brand equity (Journal of Marketing, 1993) and a live run of Zoya's school-gate test: a blind test that ends ten and ten, then a named test where sixteen of twenty parents pick Laddoo Lab. We build Keller's brand pyramid step by step (identity, meaning, response, relationship) and walk through David Aaker's five brand equity assets (Managing Brand Equity, 1991): awareness, perceived quality, associations, loyalty and other assets, with examples from an airline, a hospital, a phone maker, a bank and a snack company. We also look at the human side honestly: trust makes buying easy, but a brand takes years to build and one bad batch can break it, and under the accounting rule IAS 38 a brand you build yourself is not shown as an asset.

This is Episode 22 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
